title_en: Ep 62 - Global hedge fund outlook 2027 and investor insights, with Marex Prime Services' cap intro team
title_zh: AFI 播客 Ep 62：2027 全球对冲基金展望与投资者洞察——对话 Marex 资本引介团队
subtitle_zh: Marex 三大区资本引介专家解读 2027 对冲基金资金流、SMA 崛起与关键主题
summary_zh: 本期 AFI（Alternative Fund Insight）播客由主持人 Will Wainwright 对话 Marex Prime Services 资本引介（capital introduction）团队的三位专家：纽约的 John Service（北美视角）、香港的 Amy Chung（亚洲视角）与伦敦的 Chris Lloyd（欧洲视角），共同展望 2027 年全球对冲基金机会集。三人一致认为，经历约八年净流出后，对冲基金正重新获得各类投资者青睐：2022 年以来回报普遍回升，投资者追求低相关性（correlation）与分散化（diversification），股票与债券相关性上升进一步推动资金转向分散化策略。独立管理账户（SMA）的复兴是本集主线，它凭借透明度与资本效率（cross margining、加杠杆）改变了资金流向；但 Amy 指出亚洲家族办公室（family offices）仍以回报为先，SMA 反而抬高了集合基金（commingled fund）的募资门槛。大宗商品与宏观策略因离散度上升而走强，多管理人平台（multi-manager）也在积极招募商品人才。展望 2027，可携式阿尔法（portable alpha）、主动延展（active extension）与杠杆份额类别等资本效率主题料将延续。本集为理解全球对冲基金资金格局提供了难得的多区域一线视角。
description: Ep 62 - Global hedge fund outlook 2027 and investor insights, with Marex Prime Services' cap intro team

turns.en: Hello and welcome to the latest AFI podcast with me, Will Wainwright. I founded or turned to fund insights to provide high quality intel and insights focused on the global hedge fund world and bring the industry together at our summits and round tables. We are looking forward to doing the same in 2027.
turns.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听最新一期 AFI 播客，我是 Will Wainwright。我创办了 Alternative Fund Insight，专注于为全球对冲基金世界提供高质量的资讯与洞察，并通过我们的峰会和圆桌会议把行业凝聚在一起。我们期待在 2027 年继续做同样的事。

turns.en: So please head to alternativefundinsight.com for more information about our intel and click summits to see our 2027 calendar.
turns.zh: 所以请访问 alternativefundinsight.com 了解更多关于我们资讯产品的信息，点击 summits 查看我们的 2027 年日程。

turns.en: Whether you're a vendor, tracking hedge fund launches, a COO looking to benchmark operational excellence, an allocator scouting opportunities or many other use cases, see how AFI's intel and in-person events can raise your game next year.
turns.zh: 无论你是追踪对冲基金新发行的供应商、想为卓越运营做对标的首席运营官（COO）、寻找机会的配置者（allocator），还是其他许多用途，都可以看看 AFI 的资讯和线下活动如何帮你在明年更上一层楼。

turns.en: Speaking of which, I'm delighted on this episode to be joined by three members of Marix's 14 Strong Capital Introductions team to provide a global overview of the hedge fund opportunity set in 2027. The key trends, allocator shifts and macro talking points which are setting the agenda.
turns.zh: 说到这个，本期节目我非常高兴请到了 Marex 那支 14 人的资本引介（capital introduction）团队的三位成员，为我们提供 2027 年全球对冲基金投资机会集的全景概览：正在设定议程的关键趋势、配置者的转变，以及宏观层面的讨论焦点。

turns.en: We are seeing high interest in hedge funds from all investor types, making this a key moment of opportunity. And in the next 25 minutes, you'll receive a unique overview to help you prepare for what's next.
turns.zh: 我们看到各类投资者对对冲基金的兴趣都很高涨，这使其成为一个关键的机遇时刻。在接下来的 25 分钟里，你将听到一份独特的全景概览，帮你为接下来的变化做好准备。

turns.en: Now to the podcast, I'm delighted to bring in Marix's capintro specialist, John Service, speaking from New York and providing the North America perspective. Amy Chung in Hong Kong with the Asia overview and Chris Lloyd in London to discuss the European perspective on this special podcast episode.
turns.zh: 现在进入正题。我很高兴请来了 Marex 的资本引介专家 John Service，他在纽约为我们提供北美视角；Amy Chung 在香港带来亚洲概览；还有 Chris Lloyd 在伦敦，为我们解读欧洲视角，共同参与本期特别节目。

turns.en: John, Amy, Chris, it's great to have you on, so thank you for joining me today and I'd like to start off by asking about that positive momentum that we are seeing. John, I'll start with you. It'd be great to get your insights on the ground there in North America.
turns.zh: John、Amy、Chris，非常高兴你们能来，感谢你们今天来陪我聊。我想先从我们正在看到的这股积极势头聊起。John，我先问你，很想听听你在北美的第一线观察。

turns.en: What is driving the renewed interest and the flows that we're seeing this year? Yeah, so I think what you had over the last call it eight years was negative flows into the hedge fund group. So from 2016 to 2019, 2020 to 2023, the net flows were negative and it was also a low period for returns.
turns.zh: 今年是什么在推动对冲基金兴趣的回暖和资金流入？是的，我觉得过去大约八年里，对冲基金这个资产类别整体是资金净流出的。从 2016 到 2019、2020 到 2023，净流量都是负的，那段时间回报也处于低位。

turns.en: And what we've seen is after 2022, we've seen an increase to returns in general, virtually every class is up. And I think from that, you've seen a push into hedge funds. Now, it's not the only thing, right? So there's always multiple drivers.
turns.zh: 而我们看到的是，2022 年之后回报普遍开始回升，几乎每一类资产都在上涨。我觉得正是这一点，推动了资金重新涌入对冲基金。当然，这并不是唯一的原因，对吧？背后的驱动因素从来都是多元的。

turns.en: And then on top of that, we've seen the environment change, right? So, so we've seen certain other strategies. We've seen an increase in their opportunities set to get better dispersion has increased out there and and hedge funds tend to give you a less correlated return stream and the investors want that.
turns.zh: 在此之上，市场环境也发生了变化，对吧？我们看到某些其他策略的机会集在扩大，市场离散度（dispersion）在上升，而对冲基金往往能给你一条相关性更低的回报流，这正是投资者想要的。

turns.en: Yeah, great. So that idea of diversification and correlated returns alongside the liquidity that hedge funds offer seems seems to be a kind of key theme at the moment. Let me put that over to you, Amy, in a pack, be great to hear what you're seeing.
turns.zh: 好，很好。所以分散化和低相关回报这个思路，加上对冲基金提供的流动性，似乎是当下的一个核心主题。我把话题交给亚太的 Amy，很想听听你那边的观察。

turns.en: So what I'm seeing in Asia is definitely more engagement with hedge funds. And I think what's interesting is actually why so strong performance has obviously helped.
turns.zh: 我在亚洲看到的是，大家对对冲基金的参与度明显更高了。我觉得有意思的其实是背后的原因——强劲的业绩表现当然是有帮助的。

turns.en: And allocators are also becoming more deliberate about the role in which hedge funds play in the overall portfolio. So I'm seeing family offices, increasing allocations and hedge funds.
turns.zh: 配置者也开始更有意识地去思考，对冲基金在整个投资组合里应该扮演什么角色。所以我看到家族办公室（family offices）在加大对对冲基金的配置。

turns.en: And there's definitely more discussions around correlation and portfolio fit rather than just do I like this manager, you know, are we close enough is he going to be managing my money well.
turns.zh: 讨论的焦点也更多地转向相关性（correlation）和组合契合度，而不只是“我喜不喜欢这个基金经理、我们合不合得来、他能不能帮我把钱管好”。

turns.en: And I'm also seeing investors asking whether or not the manager provides something that they cannot get cheaply through beta. So, yeah, we're really seeing a lot of positive momentum in the hedge fund industry in Asia and allocating to global hedge funds as well. Great. Thanks, Amy and Chris, is that mirror what you're seeing?
turns.zh: 我还看到投资者在问，这个管理人提供的东西，是不是自己没法通过便宜的贝塔（beta）就拿到。所以是的，我们确实看到亚洲的对冲基金行业有着非常积极的势头，资金也在配置到全球对冲基金上。很好，谢谢 Amy。Chris，你看到的是同样的情况吗？

turns.en: Yeah, exactly. So I think my colleagues have covered most of the points I was going to make. I think just overall it's the other comment I make is the previous asset classes that are in favor have become out of every little bit.
turns.zh: 是的，完全一致。我觉得同事们已经把我大部分要讲的点都覆盖了。我要补充的一点是，之前那些受宠的资产类别，如今正在一点点失宠。

turns.en: So sort of private credit would be one that you could point to were people were making significant commitments. And I think that has softened a little bit and distributions are coming back from those which has supported kind of the hedge funds as an asset class that can perform for you.
turns.zh: 比如私募信贷（private credit）就是一个例子，之前大家在那里做了大量的出资承诺。我觉得现在热度有点降温，分配（distributions）也开始回流，这反而支撑了对冲基金作为一个能为你创造业绩的资产类别的地位。

turns.en: That can give you sort of fixed income like returns without duration risk, absolutely returns are there now because often these products are kind of a rate plus products.
turns.zh: 它能给你类似固定收益的回报，却没有久期风险（duration risk），绝对回报现在也在那里，因为这些产品很多本质上是“利率加成”型（rate plus）的产品。

turns.en: So now you're seeing hedge funds generally speaking like allocators looking to achieve every 10% a year and I think you can do that in hedge funds now on a reliable basis. Amy, are there particular strategies that you see is coming back into fashion in APAC?
turns.zh: 所以现在你会看到，配置者普遍想在对冲基金里拿到 10% 左右的年化回报，我觉得现在已经能够可靠地做到这一点了。Amy，在亚太有没有哪些策略你看到正在重新流行起来？

turns.en: Yeah, so I think what's really interesting is after July, so we saw major pull back in the market and from that point we're seeing investors asking are they overexposed in equities and particularly in AI.
turns.zh: 有，我觉得很有意思的是，7 月之后市场出现过一次大幅回调，从那以后我们看到投资者在问，自己是不是在股票上、尤其是在 AI 上敞口过大。

turns.en: So as a result, we're seeing an uptick of interest in genuine diversifiers, anything from market neutral RV, macro, these kind of strategies do come up a lot.
turns.zh: 结果就是，大家对真正意义上的分散化工具兴趣上升，市场中性（market neutral）、相对价值（RV）、宏观（macro）这类策略被提及得非常频繁。

turns.en: But then at the same time, they're also looking for the true alpha specialists in which you really require a manager's expertise and skill sets to manage that kind of that sort of bucket.
turns.zh: 但与此同时，他们也在寻找真正的阿尔法（alpha）专家——那种确实需要依靠管理人的专业能力和技巧才能驾驭的领域。

turns.en: So some strategies that I'm seeing that is in vogue include biotech, US small mid cap because you really need to be on the ground to collect the kind of information and activist strategies as well. And also I think one important thing is around commodities in which we can explore down the line.
turns.zh: 我看到当红的策略包括生物科技（biotech）、美国中小盘（US small mid cap），因为你真的需要扎根当地才能收集到那类信息，还有维权投资者（activist）策略。另外我觉得很重要的一点是大宗商品（commodities），这个我们可以稍后展开聊。

turns.en: Yeah, great. John, I'll move on to you now. So you know, you touched on which strategies you are seeing as those that have kind of come back and what are the factors behind this.
turns.zh: 好，很好。John，我现在转向你。你刚才谈到了哪些策略正在回暖，以及背后的因素是什么。

turns.en: Resurgence in hedge fund interest at the same time we've seen a real renaissance in the use of separately managed accounts that has changed the nature of capital flows into established firms and also emerging funds. So give us your take on the SMA trend.
turns.zh: 在对冲基金兴趣重燃的同时，我们也看到独立管理账户（separately managed accounts，SMA）的使用迎来了一场真正的复兴，这改变了资金流向成熟机构以及新兴基金的方式。所以请谈谈你对 SMA 趋势的看法。

turns.en: Yeah, we've seen over the last five years, I would say we've seen a definite increase to that. I think it's, I think it's somewhat multifaceted. The allocators have become more sophisticated.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得过去五年里，这方面确实出现了明显的增长。原因是多重的。首先，配置者变得更成熟老练了。

turns.en: The providers, PBs and everybody technology has increased allowing these groups to set up these managed accounts monitor them and keep them going much more effectively. And then, and then third tier for the for the larger groups that can actually do this. It's a better use of capital, right. And so, so they can get cross margining.
turns.zh: 其次，服务提供商、主经纪商（PB）以及整个行业的技术水平都在提升，让这些机构能够更高效地设立、监控并持续运营这些管理账户。第三，对那些真正有能力做这件事的大型机构来说，这是更好的资本使用方式，对吧？他们可以实现交叉保证金（cross margining）。

turns.en: They can effectively lever up, right. And so that capital usage allows them to do other things within their portfolio in that overall construction. And you know, this is a global trend that we're seeing. Let me put the same question to Chris on the SMAs.
turns.zh: 他们可以有效地加杠杆，对吧？这种资本使用效率让他们能在整体组合构建中去做别的事情。要知道，这是一个全球性的趋势。我把同样的问题抛给 Chris，谈谈 SMA。

turns.en: Yeah, I mean, it's becoming sort of very prevalent at prevalence. So I think to sort of John's point, the sort of infrastructure is now there that people can do this. It's kind of much cheaper costs. So you don't necessarily have to be as large as you used to be.
turns.zh: 是的，我是说，它正变得非常普遍。所以就像 John 说的，现在基础设施已经到位，大家都能做这件事了，成本也低了很多，所以你不必再像以前那样规模很大才行。

turns.en: And then secondly, I think managers are much more willing to accept to SMA capital than they used to be. So it makes it easy. I mean, some managers essentially only build businesses of SMAs.
turns.zh: 其次，我觉得管理人现在也比以前更愿意接受 SMA 资金了。所以这让事情变得容易。我是说，有些管理人基本上就是靠 SMA 建起整个业务的。

turns.en: So we're seeing a sort of a big increase there. We're seeing loads and loads of loads from kind of large sort of quantum groups, which are looking to kind of get their sort of fundamental exposure and sort of sweat that capital into this fundamental managers.
turns.zh: 所以我们看到这块出现了大幅增长。我们看到来自大型量化机构（quant groups）的巨量资金，他们想获得基本面敞口，把资本投给这些基本面管理人。

turns.en: We're seeing traditional investors that would have gone into chemical funds, setting up SMAs and then also boxing products of SMAs, so sort of almost like many multi strats, but it's a product of SMAs.
turns.zh: 我们也看到传统投资者——过去他们会投集合基金（commingled funds）——现在设立 SMA，甚至把 SMA 打包成产品，有点像多策略基金（multi-strats），但本质是一篮子 SMA 产品。

turns.en: So I think it's sort of prevalent everywhere and it has a big impact then on those people setting up businesses as certain types of strategies lend themselves very well to SMAs. And then there's a lot of capital then available to those groups and then certainly don't.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这个趋势无处不在，而且对那些正在创业建业务的人影响很大，因为某些类型的策略非常适合做 SMA，于是大量资本就流向了这些机构，而那些不适合做 SMA 的则……

turns.en: And so for a given level of talent, where one where capital is more abundant, they're able to raise and I think where it's not SMAable. It's actually it's actually hard to raise.
turns.zh: 所以在同等人才水平下，资本充裕的地方他们就能募到钱；而我认为，不适合做 SMA 的策略，实际上募资反而更难了。

turns.en: Yeah, just to drill into that, you know, there are so many headlines and so many prime brokerage surveys about the big headline flows into the hedge fund space at the moment.
turns.zh: 是的，我想深入追问一下。现在有那么多头条新闻，还有那么多主经纪商调查，都在讲当下资金大量涌入对冲基金领域。

turns.en: But you know, raising capital is never easy, you know, never has been an even in this environment, you know, for a lot of hedge funds and emerging hedge funds, it is a challenge.
turns.zh: 但你知道，募资从来都不容易，一直都是如此，即便在当前环境下，对很多对冲基金尤其是新兴对冲基金来说，仍然是个挑战。

turns.en: And it is interesting because with SMAs, you can get going quite quickly, but it is obviously different to building up a commingled vehicle, which takes more time, but has a different kind of end point. So it'd be great to get a bit more take on how you see the difference between the two when you're building a business.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，SMA 让你能很快起步，但这跟搭建一个集合投资载体（commingled vehicle）显然是不同的路径，后者需要更多时间，但终点也不一样。所以很想多听听你们的看法：在建业务时，你们如何看待这两者之间的区别？

turns.en: Yeah, I think ultimately if you only have one SMA, then you're not that far off from just essentially being an employee of the business you've got the SMA for.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得归根结底，如果你只有一个 SMA，那你跟给这个 SMA 客户打工基本上没太大区别。

turns.en: Obviously with optionality on the upside to get additional one. So I think you only really start to diversify yourself and become sort of a true like business in that sense, once you can get multiple SMAs.
turns.zh: 当然，你有上行选择权（optionality），可以争取更多账户。所以我觉得，只有拿到多个 SMA，你才真正开始分散自己、成为真正意义上的“业务”。

turns.en: So typically what we'll see is groups will will look to get multiple SMAs and ideally have a mixture of different types of groups that are giving those SMAs, so the risk limits are different.
turns.zh: 通常我们看到的是，机构会争取拿到多个 SMA，而且理想情况下，这些 SMA 来自不同类型的机构，这样风险限额也不一样。

turns.en: And then also look to launch a commingled fund alongside that. So that commingled fund could be seated by partner capsule, it could be seated by friends of family capsule, it could be seated by a seed error or some strategic investors.
turns.zh: 然后他们也会同时发起一只集合基金。这只集合基金可以由合伙人资本做种子，可以由朋友和家人资本做种子，也可以由种子投资者或某些战略投资者做种子。

turns.en: Or you could just start it quite small, but the idea is you kind of grow that pool of capsule as well alongside and then you end up in a position there where you have kind of a nice diversified business with less pin risk. Yeah, yeah. Great. Amy, the SMA trend looks pretty strong in Asia as well. What are you seeing on the ground there?
turns.zh: 或者你也可以从小规模起步，但思路是，在 SMA 之外同步培育这个资金池，最终你会处在一个很好的位置：拥有一个多元化、集中风险（pin risk）更低的业务。好，很好。Amy，SMA 趋势在亚洲看起来也很强劲，你在当地看到的情况如何？

turns.en: Yeah, sure. So I think obviously SMAs are great for managers because it can help them grow the firm, but then the investors that I speak to, so a lot of these are Asian family offices who often start with 2 to 5 million tickets and they would only be investing in the commingled fund.
turns.zh: 是的，当然。我觉得 SMA 对管理人来说当然很好，因为能帮他们把公司做大。但我接触到的投资者——其中很多是亚洲家族办公室——通常都是从 200 万到 500 万美元的投资额起步，而且他们往往只愿意投集合基金。

turns.en: Unless there is a really compelling reason to invest in the fund, they don't want to be the first one to invest and what's really important to them is to see the track and the scale.
turns.zh: 除非有特别有说服力的理由去投那只基金，否则他们不想做第一个吃螃蟹的人。对他们来说，真正重要的是看到业绩记录（track record）和规模。

turns.en: So sometimes we see managers running SMAs that are quite different to their original strategy, you know, not running in piracy. So it becomes kind of difficult for the fund managers to be raising money for the commingled fund that is different to the SMA.
turns.zh: 所以有时候我们会看到，管理人运营的 SMA 跟他们原本的策略相当不同，比如并不是同一种打法。这样一来，基金经理要为一个跟 SMA 风格不一致的集合基金募资，反而变得困难。

turns.en: So anyway, I'm actually seeing the bar for commingled funds moving higher. So nowadays it's quite typical to hear minimum size of 100 million in the fund. So ironically, SMAs can help scale the firm without necessarily making it easier for the commingled fund to raise money.
turns.zh: 总之，我实际上看到集合基金的门槛在不断抬高。如今听到“基金最低规模 1 亿美元”已经相当普遍。所以讽刺的是，SMA 能帮机构扩大体量，却不一定能让集合基金更容易募到钱。

turns.en: Yeah, interesting. And just sticking with you, Amy, you know, are there any differences that you've seen in Asia in terms of how allocators are viewing hedge funds, you know, obviously we've noted there is more enthusiasm.
turns.zh: 有意思。还是想问问你，Amy。在亚洲，配置者看待对冲基金的方式有没有什么不同之处？我们当然已经注意到热情更高了。

turns.en: This is a global trend, but in terms of, you know, specific invested types or anything else that you're seeing, which is slightly different in Asia. Yeah, sure. So I think it's definitely dominated by a lot of Asian family offices. It's still a growing part.
turns.zh: 这是一个全球性趋势，但就具体的投资者类型或你在亚洲看到的其他方面而言，有没有什么略显不同的地方？是的，当然。我觉得这块主要还是由大量亚洲家族办公室主导的，而且这部分仍在增长。

turns.en: There are a lot of first generation family offices, you know, people who make money from crypto, you know, we're seeing a lot of them popping up in Hong Kong and Singapore. And I think what's really common in the Asian family office space is we like to talk about returns returns always come first.
turns.zh: 有很多第一代家族办公室，比如靠加密货币（crypto）赚到钱的人，我们在香港和新加坡看到很多这样的办公室在涌现。我觉得亚洲家族办公室圈子里很共通的一点是，我们喜欢谈回报——回报永远排第一。

turns.en: Then it's the investment processes and then the pedigree the track and so on and so forth. And then one thing I have to say is that allocators are definitely more thoughtful about correlation and what hedge fund plays in the overall portfolio.
turns.zh: 其次才是投资流程，然后是团队背景、业绩记录等等。还有一点我得说，配置者现在确实更用心地在考虑相关性，以及对冲基金在整体组合里扮演的角色。

turns.en: But still, you know, a lot of conversations still start up with what are their returns. So yeah, anyway, so portfolio construction is becoming more sophisticated. That's for sure, but I just wouldn't underestimate how important returns are for the region. Yeah, they are still the key, the key driver, the key determinant.
turns.zh: 但即便如此，很多对话还是从“你们的回报是多少”开始。所以是的，总之，组合构建正变得更成熟，这一点毫无疑问，但别低估回报对这个地区的重要性——是的，它仍然是关键驱动因素，是关键的决定性因素。

turns.en: The other thing we're seeing people do on the commingled side to sort of counter one of the main reasons why people do SMAs is leverage your glasses. So just a direct one or half times or two times leverage your glass that allows those smaller investors to pretty much get most of the benefits from a returns perspective.
turns.zh: 另一个我们看到大家在集合基金这边做的事，是用来应对人们做 SMA 的一个主要原因——杠杆份额类别（leveraged share classes）。就是直接发行 1 倍、1.5 倍或 2 倍杠杆的份额类别，让规模较小的投资者从回报角度也能拿到 SMA 的大部分好处。

turns.en: You would get by the SMA. So you don't have the transparency and all that other stuff, but to him is point returns all the key focus. Yeah, great. Thanks Chris. John, coming to you North America is still the capital of this industry in terms of the size of hedge funds.
turns.zh: 虽然你没有了透明度以及其他那些东西，但对他们来说，重点是回报，回报才是核心关注点。很好，谢谢 Chris。John，回到你这边。就对冲基金的规模而言，北美仍然是这个行业的中心。

turns.en: The flows coming from new pensions, endowments, other institutional allocators, family offices to give me your take on the different investor types that are kind of driving that continued dominance in America.
turns.zh: 资金来自新兴的养老金、捐赠基金（endowments）、其他机构配置者、家族办公室。请谈谈你的看法：是哪些不同的投资者类型在推动美国这种持续的支配地位？

turns.en: Yeah, so if you take a step back, obviously we had the liquidity issue where everything sort of went upside down and you had the endowments and foundations and pensions sort of had to take a step back and not being engaged in allocating the hedge fund market because they were, you know, basically managing their private portfolios.
turns.zh: 是的，如果你退一步看，之前我们显然经历了流动性问题，一切都天翻地覆，捐赠基金、基金会和养老金不得不先退一步，没能积极参与对冲基金市场的配置，因为他们基本上都在忙着打理自己的私募投资组合。

turns.en: We have started to see flows there, which is great. And now we've seen a resurgence of engagement from the endowments and foundations, family offices less so they didn't have the same exact problems that those institutes, the other institutional investors had.
turns.zh: 我们已经开始看到那边有资金流回来了，这很好。现在我们又看到捐赠基金和基金会的参与度重新回升，家族办公室则没那么明显——他们没有遭遇那些机构投资者所遇到的同样问题。

turns.en: They have been somewhat of a constant little bit of ebb and flow, but they definitely have been a constant out there the first half of this year. We definitely saw a lot of movement in the middle portion of the year.
turns.zh: 它们一直算是比较稳定的存在，有些许潮起潮落，但绝对是市场上的一支常备力量。今年上半年，我们肯定看到年中那段时间有很多动作。

turns.en: There was a drawback and now we're starting to see a resurgence again of capital that's going to be allocated towards the end of the year.
turns.zh: 先是经历了一段回撤，现在我们又开始看到资金的重新涌入，这些资金会在年底前配置出去。

turns.en: So a lot of that capital is going to diverse fires, a bit of larger managers, but as we had spoken about before with the SMA land, the SMA allows allocators to move much earlier due to the transparency and the ability to take the business risks off the table.
turns.zh: 所以大量资金流向了分散化策略，也有一部分流向较大的管理人。但正如我们之前谈到的 SMA 领域，SMA 凭借其透明度和把业务风险排除在外的能力，让配置者能够更早行动。

turns.en: So that has been a fairly large boom to movement of capital, although it depends on the strategy as to where those allocators are going to go. Yeah, yeah. And John just changing text slightly, commodity strategies have really stood out, you know, particularly in the last few weeks actually.
turns.zh: 所以这对资金流动形成了相当大的助推，不过具体流向还要看策略。好的好的。John，稍微换个话题，大宗商品策略真的非常突出，尤其是最近这几周。

turns.en: So they seem to really remain a strong area of growth in this industry. Yeah, we've definitely seen that actually even all of the last year and a half, there's been quite a pick up in the interest for those types of strategies. Obviously, merits were heavily involved there, so that's very nice.
turns.zh: 它们似乎仍然是这个行业里增长强劲的领域。是的，我们确实看到了，实际上过去一年半以来，对这类策略的兴趣一直在明显升温。显然，Marex 也深度参与其中，所以这非常好。

turns.en: But one of the one of the drivers behind that and macro as well is that equity and fixed income correlations have gone up dramatically over the last two and a half years. And so you've seen a shift to the diverse fire class as it would be and the returns are there.
turns.zh: 但背后的驱动因素之一——宏观策略也是如此——是股票和固定收益之间的相关性在过去两年半里大幅上升。所以你看到资金转向了分散化那一类资产，而且回报也确实存在。

turns.en: So there's a lot of dispersion on the geopolitical environment and world environment has set itself up so that these strategies can take advantage of all that movement. Yeah, yeah, great. Thanks, John Chris, do you want to pick up on the commodities thread?
turns.zh: 地缘政治环境和全球环境本身就充满了离散度，而这些策略恰好能利用所有这些波动获利。好的好的，很好，谢谢 John。Chris，你想不想接着谈谈大宗商品这条线？

turns.en: Yeah, absolutely. I think we're seeing a lot of demand there when investors, I would say for the reasons that John described. And then we're seeing new launches in the space as well, which is nice to see. So we've had some new launches come out of sort of larger sort of pod shops.
turns.zh: 当然想。我觉得我们在那块看到投资者的需求非常大，原因就如 John 所说。而且我们还看到这个领域不断有新的基金发行，这很令人欣喜。我们看到一些新的发行来自规模较大的多投资经理平台（pod shops）。

turns.en: We've had some new launches out of kind of commodity houses, different kind of groups. But overall, what I would say is that when these launches come out pretty much every investor will at least take a look at them.
turns.zh: 我们也看到一些新的发行来自大宗商品交易机构，是不同类型的机构。但总的来说，我想说的是，每当这些新产品发行出来，几乎每个投资者都愿意至少看一看。

turns.en: And then often it becomes sort of a capacity issue on these because depending on what commodities they're trading capacity can be a big consideration. And then if there's a lot of demand for that product, you can often see some of these launch with quite a lot of their total capacity taken up on sort of day one or day two.
turns.zh: 然后往往会变成一个容量问题，因为取决于他们交易的是什么大宗商品，容量可能是一个很大的考量因素。如果某个产品需求旺盛，你常常会看到这些新基金在第一天或第二天就已经被认购掉了相当大的总容量。

turns.en: Yeah, yeah. Are they me the same in Asia? Yeah, I think there's a lot of interest for commodities for sure. And a lot of allocators are under allocated in the space. Actually, that's more of a global phenomenon rather than just Asia.
turns.zh: 好的好的。Amy，亚洲的情况也一样吗？是的，我觉得对大宗商品的兴趣肯定很浓。而且很多配置者在这个领域是配置不足的。实际上，这更是一个全球性现象，而不仅仅是亚洲。

turns.en: So yeah, we're seeing a lot of them mapping out the universe and they're ideally looking for managers that can trade multiple commodities. But it's actually quite hard to find. A lot of them have probably gone too big than they don't want it.
turns.zh: 所以我们看到很多人在梳理整个投资范围，他们理想中想找的是能交易多种大宗商品的管理人。但这其实很难找。很多这类管理人可能已经规模过大，不愿意再接新资金。

turns.en: A lot of them might be very small, just managing 20 to 30 million and yet multiple SMAs at the same time. So it is a very difficult allocation. And at the same time, I'm also noticing that the multi manager platforms in my region are actively sourcing for commodities talent.
turns.zh: 还有很多可能规模非常小，只管理着 2000 万到 3000 万美元，却同时运营着多个 SMA。所以这是一笔很难做的配置。与此同时，我也注意到，我们地区的多管理人平台（multi-manager platforms）正在积极招募大宗商品人才。

turns.en: So demand is coming from both sides. Yeah, for the funds and for the people. Yeah, great. Thanks, AB. And as I mentioned at the stars, we are less than two months from the end of the year now. The hedge fund industry is at a record size. We've seen continued positive allocator sentiment.
turns.zh: 所以需求来自两个方向——既是为基金，也是为人才。很好，谢谢 Amy。正如我开场时提到的，现在距离年底已经不到两个月了。对冲基金行业的规模已经创下历史新高，我们也看到配置者情绪持续向好。

turns.en: It'd be great to hear from each of you on your priorities going into next year. Whether there are any particular trends or themes that you'd like to focus on. And what should those in the hedge fund industry be thinking about as we go into 2027? I'm going to start with you, John.
turns.zh: 很想听听你们每一位在进入明年时的优先事项，有没有哪些特别的趋势或主题是你们想重点关注的，以及在我们迈入 2027 年之际，对冲基金行业的人应该思考些什么。我先从你开始，John。

turns.en: Obviously, we've had a bit of backup in the equity markets and on the credit side. Probably a good thing. They were getting a little overstretched. And so what I would say is. I think equities remain the predominant class. I think that going into next year, they should continue to remain to be the predominant class.
turns.zh: 显然，我们在股票市场和信贷端都经历了一些回调，这大概是件好事，之前有点过度拉伸了。所以我想说的是，我认为股票仍然是主导性的资产类别，我觉得进入明年，它们应该会继续保持主导地位。

turns.en: So what we also see is that more allocators focus on sort of the wings. So long only and market neutral, trying to isolate alpha and not pay for beta effectively. That's what that trade is. I think that that trend will continue. I don't see you debating. And then, you know, on top of that, obviously, Amy had mentioned earlier on.
turns.zh: 我们还看到，更多配置者开始关注“两翼”——纯多头（long only）和市场中性，试图分离出阿尔法（alpha），而不是为贝塔（beta）付费，这就是那笔交易的本质。我觉得这个趋势会延续，我看不到有什么会改变它。除此之外，就像 Amy 之前提到的，

turns.en: We continue to see interest in healthcare, biotech, TMT. And I think that's going to continue that that that is not going to go away at abs and it flows. But consistently, that remains to be out there as well. I don't see the geopolitical and macro environment changing. And so I think macro sets up to be a good trade.
turns.zh: 我们持续看到资金对医疗健康、生物科技、TMT 的兴趣。我觉得这会延续下去，不会消失——资产规模和资金流会有波动，但这类兴趣始终都在。我看不到地缘政治和宏观环境会发生变化，所以我认为宏观策略也会是一笔不错的交易。

turns.en: As well. And then also as we just recently spoke about was commodities, right. That continues to be a good class, whether a credit will will get better. Yeah. And just one word, John, you're there in America, you know, the capital of AI.
turns.zh: 还有，就是我们刚刚谈到的大宗商品，对吧？它继续是一个不错的资产类别，至于信贷会不会变得更好，我们拭目以待。好的。John，就一句话——你人在美国，那里是 AI 的中心。

turns.en: And there's so much talk about how AI is being used by hedge funds on the operational side and to generate alpha as well. How do you see that aspect of the market in the business? Yeah, I think it's still pretty nascent. I think it's a great tool for for gathering and combining and assimilating information for use.
turns.zh: 关于对冲基金如何在运营端以及创造阿尔法方面使用 AI，讨论非常多。你如何看待市场的这一面，以及对业务的影响？是的，我觉得这仍然处于相当初期的阶段。我认为它是一个很好的工具，可以用来收集、整合并消化信息以供使用。

turns.en: And then you can think about what that means. So I still think that that trumps what AI can, you know, produce from an alpha perspective. What I do feel that it can do effectively today, maybe not so many years ago, but today is that you have less of a need to start.
turns.zh: 然后你可以去思考这些信息意味着什么。所以我仍然认为，这一点胜过 AI 本身在阿尔法层面能产出的东西。我确实觉得，它今天能够有效做到的——也许几年前还不行，但今天可以——是你不再那么需要派出初级

turns.en: Analysts to go gather that information and you can now utilize AI and be quite effective at that now, depending on how you're utilizing it together information. Maybe there's some edge out there in doing that, but you know that I think that remains to be seen. I still think it resides with the PM and how they're able to utilize that info.
turns.zh: 分析师去收集那些信息，你现在可以利用 AI 相当高效地完成这件事，具体取决于你如何使用它来整合信息。也许这样做能带来某种优势，但是否如此，我觉得还有待观察。我仍然认为，关键在于投资经理（PM）以及他们如何利用这些信息。

turns.en: Amy, let me ask the same question to you. What's on your mind going into 2027? Yeah, I think just two things in general. So number one is, is the flow into hedge funds sustainable or has this year just in a strong fundraising cycle?
turns.zh: Amy，让我把同样的问题抛给你。进入 2027 年，你在想些什么？是的，我觉得总体上有两件事。第一，资金流入对冲基金是否可持续，还是说今年只是碰上了一个强劲的募资周期？

turns.en: I think that will be very interesting to see for next year. And then the next thing is, what is the next trade after AI? Is it still going to be AI itself or is it rather the things that are required to support it? Great. Thank you, Amy and Chris. What's on your mind going into 2027?
turns.zh: 我觉得这一点明年会非常值得关注。第二件事是，AI 之后的下一笔交易是什么？还会是 AI 本身，还是说更多是支撑 AI 所需的那些东西？很好，谢谢你，Amy。Chris，进入 2027 年，你在想些什么？

turns.en: Yes, I think what's on my mind in terms of what allocators have been thinking about is generally like you've got to this point of the year. It's what have you been trying to achieve in your portfolio? Have you achieved that? But it's getting close to kind of we have to start again. So next year is kind of the next thing.
turns.zh: 是的，我觉得就配置者今年到目前为止一直在思考的问题而言，核心是：你在自己的组合里想实现什么目标？你实现了吗？但现在已接近尾声，一切要重新开始，所以明年就是下一个课题。

turns.en: So I would say like some of the kind of the key bits is around like strategies I would say that can generate returns of 10% plus. I would say lowly correlated strategies again or stuff that we're seeing a lot of interest in.
turns.zh: 所以我想说，一些关键点在于策略，我会说是那些能产生 10% 以上回报的策略，还有低相关性策略，这些也是我们看到需求非常旺盛的领域。

turns.en: And then I'm seeing like a lot of people ask about sort of two times share classes. I'm seeing a lot of people ask about active extension or portable alpha products as well. And so again, it's all about it all comes down to a core thing of kind of how can we sweat this capital more?
turns.zh: 然后我看到很多人在问 2 倍杠杆份额类别（two times share classes），还有很多人在问主动延展（active extension）或可携式阿尔法（portable alpha）产品。所以归根结底，核心都是同一个问题：我们如何把这份资本用得更充分？

turns.en: And are there any inefficiencies or are there any high grading things that we can do in the portfolio to account that extra 50, 150 basis points next year? That's really interesting, Chris. And just to pick up on that, you know, the capital efficiency theme has been huge as decade in the world of higher interest rates.
turns.zh: 有没有哪些低效之处，或者我们能在组合里做哪些“择优提升”的操作，来在明年额外争取到那 50 到 150 个基点（basis points）？这真的很有意思，Chris。就着这一点来说，资本效率这个主题在过去十年这个高利率世界里影响巨大。

turns.en: It's driven the resurgence in managed accounts that we're seeing and it's making its presence felt in lots of other areas as well. I'd love to get you all take on the portable alpha theme, which has been a really strong theme this year. You see it continuing into 2027. What kind of form do you think that will take?
turns.zh: 它推动了我们正在看到的独立管理账户的复兴，也在很多其他领域发挥着影响力。我很想听听你们对可携式阿尔法这个主题的看法，这是今年一个非常强劲的主题。你觉得它会延续到 2027 年吗？会以什么样的形式呈现？

turns.en: So I think I would put that I put that together with active long only an active extension because ultimately if you take a step back, what are you trying to do with that?
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，我会把可携式阿尔法和主动纯多头（active long only）、主动延展放在一起讨论，因为归根结底，退一步看，你到底想用它们做什么？

turns.en: What you're trying to do is take capital that you have exposure to say passive equity index or something else and you're trying to essentially achieve alpha on top of that.
turns.zh: 你要做的是，把那些已经有敞口的资本——比如被动股票指数或其他东西——拿过来，然后试图在此之上叠加阿尔法。

turns.en: And so I would when we're looking at it, we're looking at sort of certain active managers, which can consistently be a passive benchmark and they're only paid about that benchmark on active extension.
turns.zh: 所以我们在看的时候，看的是某些能持续跑赢被动基准的主动管理人，而他们的收费只是按基准水平来收的。主动延展（active extension）也是类似的概念。

turns.en: It's a similar kind of concept, mostly using leverage on portable alpha. It's a similar concept. So how stability, I'll be you can generate. And then you can put that against a reference index that's what you want to do in your portfolio anyway.
turns.zh: 可携式阿尔法（portable alpha）也是类似的思路，主要是使用杠杆：看你能生成多稳定的阿尔法，然后把它叠加到一个参照指数之上，而这个参照指数本来就是你想在组合里持有的。

turns.en: And hopefully like the underwriting there is really that over a one to three year view or a two to five year view, you can outperform what you've taken out the portfolio. So that's why I think we're seeing interest. Great. Well, Chris, thanks for that.
turns.zh: 而这里的承销（underwriting）逻辑真正在于，从一到三年或两到五年的视角看，你能跑赢你从组合里拿出来的那部分资产。所以这就是我们看到兴趣所在的原因。很好，谢谢 Chris。

turns.en: John and Amy to absolutely brilliant to have you on and provide those thoughts going into next year on the flows picture in the hedge funds base and the key themes that should be on everyone's mind as we look ahead to the next 12 months. So thank you very much. Thanks a lot.
turns.zh: John 和 Amy，非常高兴你们能来，为我们提供了这些关于明年资金流格局、对冲基金基础以及展望接下来 12 个月每个人都应关注的关键主题的思考。非常感谢你们。多谢多谢。

turns.en: That's it for now. Thank you to John, Amy and Chris for more information. Please head to Marrix's website. Please see the link in the show notes and remember that early in December, we are also relating a special report building on the points made in this podcast.
turns.zh: 本期节目就到这里。感谢 John、Amy 和 Chris。欲了解更多信息，请访问 Marex 的官网，链接见节目备注。另外请记住，12 月初我们还将发布一份特别报告，在本期播客观点的基础上进一步展开。

turns.en: Head to AFI and Marrix's websites linked in feeds and emails for more information. And we'll see you next time on the AFI podcast.
turns.zh: 请访问 feeds 和邮件中链接的 AFI 和 Marex 官网以获取更多信息。我们下期 AFI 播客再见。

turns.en: This podcast is brought to you in association with Sitco, the leading asset servicer with over two trillion dollars of assets under administration and the top hedge fund administrator on the AFI 250 research ranking.
turns.zh: 本播客由 Citco 联合呈现。Citco 是领先的资产服务机构，管理资产规模超过 2 万亿美元，并在 AFI 250 研究排名中位列顶级对冲基金行政管理人（hedge fund administrator）。

turns.en: Sitco acts as a true partner to its clients dedicated to developing rich long term relationships through gold standard services and industry leading technology. Head to sitco.com for more information.
